scope: Linux native fan editor, unprivileged persistent client and restricted helper: offline candidate verification only; installation and actual hardware acceptance recorded separately

checks.test_count_scope: Whole verification suites; not added repeatedly for each feature

implemented.native_editor: 16 raw duty stages and 15 rise/fall boundaries per channel; explicit supplied draft, half-percent precision, preview separate from applied receipt
implemented.helper: Fixed installed path/--serve, typed bounded JSONL, fresh random nonce, serialized monotonic request IDs, one fd per session
implemented.authorization: Read-only handshake before any Apply, ordinary-user GUI, independent polkit action, no authentication on normal telemetry or edits
implemented.liveness: Independent heartbeat, bounded nonblocking input, continuous output draining, real child wait/reap, passive UI events when automatic sampling is disabled
implemented.recovery: Explicit original-byte restore, current-transaction receipt separate from historical GET flag, primary and recovery errors retained, orphan restore only by explicit action
implemented.ownership: Read-only foreign state does not become local cleanup responsibility; exact no-acquisition proof cannot excuse an ambiguous acquire acknowledgement

verification_limits: Simulated server/backend and real unprivileged test child processes do not exercise the installed privileged helper or EC writes.
No real fan Apply/Restore, thermal/noise, suspend/resume or long-term acceptance.
Twenty-second helper heartbeat cannot cancel a blocked synchronous kernel ioctl; recovery happens after it returns.
Windows fan transport remains unsupported; target compilation is not Windows hardware compatibility.
Only the existing qualified GM6PX0X/N.1.09MRO07 kernel protocol combination can grant write capability.
This helper is scoped to the current application session, not a startup service or resume policy.

tracking.earlier_attempts: Earlier compilation, fixture, UI and tracking failures are retained privately; final success does not erase those records.
